decisions.rationale: The smallest defensible grain from evidence is (year, month, day, carrier, flight, origin, dest, sched_dep_time): all eight columns have null_rate 0.0 and together identify one scheduled departure; flight numbers alone (2994 distinct) repeat across days and carriers, so date, carrier, and route are needed. A human should measure this grain against the warehouse before approval.
The profile shows row_count 166158 with duplicate_row_rate 0.0, so no exact duplicate rows exist in bronze and no dedupe pass is applied.
Thirteen columns landed as DECIMAL(38,9) but every sampled or listed value is integral (counts, minutes, HHMM times, flight numbers, miles), so all are cast to INTEGER.
time_hour landed as VARCHAR but all 10 samples are ISO-8601 UTC timestamps with null_rate 0.0, so it is cast strictly to TIMESTAMP.

4883 rows (null_rate 0.029388) have no actual dep_time; an is_cancelled boolean is derived so consumers can exclude cancelled flights without null checks, while dep_time, dep_delay, arr_time, arr_delay, and air_time retain their nulls.

dep_time and dep_delay (null_rate 0.029388), arr_time (0.0307), and arr_delay and air_time (0.032981) are retained nullable; nulls carry meaning (cancelled or diverted flights) and no rows are dropped or imputed.
tailnum has 1521 nulls (null_rate 0.009154) and an anomalous sample value D942DN that does not match the N-prefix pattern; the column is kept as-is and left to review rather than cleansed.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are flagged is_airbyte_metadata: true and carry only capture-tool state, so all three are dropped.

purpose: silver_nyc_flights is the cleaned flight-level table for NYC-origin departures (EWR, JFK, LGA) in January through June 2013, derived from bronze.nyc_flights. It standardizes integral DECIMAL columns to INTEGER, parses time_hour into a TIMESTAMP, drops Airbyte capture metadata, and adds an is_cancelled flag, feeding downstream delay, route, and carrier analytics.
usage: Read one row per scheduled flight departure, identified by year, month, day, carrier, flight, origin, dest, and sched_dep_time. Consumers computing delay or air-time metrics must deliberately filter on is_cancelled = false (or exclude null arr_delay/air_time) because cancelled and diverted flights retain nulls in dep_time, dep_delay, arr_time, arr_delay, and air_time. dep_time, sched_dep_time, arr_time, and sched_arr_time are integer HHMM clock encodings, not durations.
limitations: Nulls are retained, not resolved: about 2.94% of rows lack dep_time/dep_delay, 3.07% lack arr_time, and 3.30% lack arr_delay/air_time, so completed-flight metrics exclude those rows. tailnum is null on 0.92% of rows and contains at least one value (D942DN) that does not match the usual N-prefix registration pattern; no tail-number cleansing was attempted. The declared grain is plausible from profile evidence but has not been measured for uniqueness against the warehouse, and no clock-drift or near-duplicate detection was applied since duplicate_row_rate is 0.0.
